topic: Flight instructor certificate: eligibility, privileges, limitations and recent experience

notes.front: What does a flight instructor certificate (CFI) authorise its holder to do?
notes.back: Conduct ground training, flight training and certain checking events, and issue related endorsements, within the certificate's limitations and ratings.
notes.explanation: A certificated flight instructor (CFI) teaches and signs off learners, but only inside the limits of their own certificate and ratings.
notes.example: Like a driving instructor's licence: it lets you teach and sign off learners, but only for the vehicle classes printed on it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.193 Flight instructor privileges (eCFR), paragraph (a)
notes.evidence: A person who holds a flight instructor certificate is authorized within the limitations of that person's flight instructor certificate and ratings to conduct ground training, flight training, certain checking events, and to issue endorsements related to
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What is a flight instructor refresher course (FIRC)?
notes.back: An FAA-approved refresher course for flight instructors; graduating from one recently is a way to establish recent experience.
notes.explanation: The advisory circular lists FIRC graduation among the methods of re-establishing flight instructor recent experience.
notes.example: Like the continuing-education course a nurse completes to keep practising, but for flight instructors.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 30.1, page 22
notes.evidence: evidence of having graduated from an FAA-approved flight instructor refresher course (FIRC) within the preceding 3 calendar months
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What is a Gold Seal flight instructor certificate?
notes.back: A flight instructor certificate bearing a distinctive gold seal, issued to instructors with a high level of flight training activity who meet special criteria.
notes.explanation: The seal marks a record of activity: sustained flight training plus criteria set out in FAA Order 8900.1.
notes.example: Like a distinction printed on a teacher's licence for a long record of pupils passing their exams.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 28, page 21
notes.evidence: Flight instructor certificates bearing distinctive gold seals are issued to flight instructors who have maintained a high level of flight training activity and who meet special criteria.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What is the minimum age for a flight instructor certificate or rating?
notes.back: 18 years.
notes.explanation: The same age rule opens the list of eligibility requirements for every flight instructor certificate or rating in subpart H.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (a)
notes.evidence: To be eligible for a flight instructor certificate or rating a person must: (a) Be at least 18 years of age;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: A 16-year-old keen on instructing wants to sit the Flight Instructor Airplane knowledge test now. Is she old enough to take the test, and to hold the certificate?
notes.back: Old enough for the test (minimum age 16), but not for the certificate, which needs 18.
notes.explanation: The Testing Matrix sets 16 as the age for this knowledge test; the certificate's own minimum under §61.183(a) stays at 18.
notes.source: FAA Airman Knowledge Testing Matrix (revised 9/25/26), "Instructor: Flight, Ground, & Sport Pilot", page 10
notes.evidence: FIA Flight Instructor Airplane 100 16 2.5 70
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: How many questions, how much time and what passing score does the Flight Instructor Airplane knowledge test have?
notes.back: 100 questions, 2.5 hours, passing score 70.
notes.explanation: The Testing Matrix lists these figures for the Flight Instructor Airplane test; they can change when the matrix is revised.
notes.source: FAA Airman Knowledge Testing Matrix (revised 9/25/26), "Instructor: Flight, Ground, & Sport Pilot", page 10
notes.evidence: FIA Flight Instructor Airplane 100 16 2.5 70
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What English language ability does a flight instructor applicant need?
notes.back: The ability to read, speak, write and understand English.
notes.explanation: If an applicant cannot meet one of these for medical reasons, the FAA may instead place operating limitations on the certificate.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (b)
notes.evidence: (b) Be able to read, speak, write, and understand the English language. If the applicant is unable to meet one of these requirements due to medical reasons, then the Administrator may place such operating limitations on that applicant's flight instructor certificate as are necessary;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Which pilot certificates can support an application for a flight instructor certificate?
notes.back: A commercial pilot certificate or an airline transport pilot certificate, with a category and class rating appropriate to the instructor rating sought.
notes.explanation: The rule names only these two grades, so no amount of flying on a private pilot certificate qualifies.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (c)(1)
notes.evidence: (c) Hold either a commercial pilot certificate or airline transport pilot certificate with: (1) An aircraft category and class rating that is appropriate to the flight instructor rating sought; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Dana holds a private pilot certificate with 600 hours, 200 of them as PIC in single-engine airplanes. She wants a flight instructor certificate with an airplane single-engine rating. What stands in her way under §61.183?
notes.back: D) She must first hold a commercial pilot or airline transport pilot certificate
notes.choices:
A) Nothing: her PIC hours are well above the minimum
B) Her age, if she is under 21
C) She needs 1,500 hours of total time
D) She must first hold a commercial pilot or airline transport pilot certificate
notes.choicesExplained: A: PIC hours do not replace the required grade of pilot certificate. C: §61.183 sets no total-time minimum; its flight-time rule is 15 hours as PIC in the category and class. B: the minimum age is 18, not 21.
notes.explanation: Eligibility starts with the grade of pilot certificate; experience on a private pilot certificate cannot stand in for it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (c)(1)
notes.evidence: (c) Hold either a commercial pilot certificate or airline transport pilot certificate with: (1) An aircraft category and class rating that is appropriate to the flight instructor rating sought; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: For which flight instructor ratings must the applicant hold an instrument rating, or equivalent privileges, on their pilot certificate?
notes.back: Airplane (single-engine or multiengine), powered-lift, and instrument instructor ratings.
notes.explanation: The rule accepts instrument privileges on the pilot certificate as well as an instrument rating; rotorcraft and glider instructor ratings are not on the list.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (c)(2)
notes.evidence: if applying for— (i) A flight instructor certificate with an airplane category and single-engine class rating; (ii) A flight instructor certificate with an airplane category and multiengine class rating; (iii) A flight instructor certificate with a powered-lift rating; or (iv) A flight instructor certificate with an instrument rating.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Sam holds a commercial pilot certificate with a rotorcraft-helicopter rating but no instrument rating. He applies for a flight instructor certificate with a helicopter rating. Does §61.183(c)(2) require an instrument rating?
notes.back: A) No: the instrument requirement lists airplane, powered-lift and instrument instructor ratings only
notes.choices:
A) No: the instrument requirement lists airplane, powered-lift and instrument instructor ratings only
B) Yes, unless he holds an airline transport pilot certificate
C) Yes: every flight instructor applicant needs one
D) No, but only if he has 15 hours as PIC in instrument conditions
notes.choicesExplained: C: the requirement is limited to the listed ratings. B: which pilot certificate he holds does not matter, because a helicopter instructor rating is not on the list. D: no such instrument-conditions rule exists; the 15 hours PIC rule is about the category and class.
notes.explanation: The paragraph names four instructor ratings, and a helicopter rating is not among them.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (c)(2)
notes.evidence: if applying for— (i) A flight instructor certificate with an airplane category and single-engine class rating; (ii) A flight instructor certificate with an airplane category and multiengine class rating; (iii) A flight instructor certificate with a powered-lift rating; or (iv) A flight instructor certificate with an instrument rating.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What endorsement on the fundamentals of instructing must a flight instructor applicant receive?
notes.back: A logbook endorsement from an authorized instructor on the §61.185 fundamentals of instructing, appropriate to the knowledge test.
notes.explanation: The endorsement ties the fundamentals-of-instructing ground training to the knowledge test the applicant will take.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (d)
notes.evidence: (d) Receive a logbook endorsement from an authorized instructor on the fundamentals of instructing listed in § 61.185 of this part appropriate to the required knowledge test;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Which instructor certificates exempt a flight instructor applicant from the Fundamentals of Instructing knowledge test?
notes.back: A flight instructor or ground instructor certificate issued under part 61.
notes.explanation: The exemption covers ground instructor certificates as well as flight instructor certificates.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (e)(1)
notes.evidence: (e) Pass a knowledge test on the areas listed in § 61.185(a)(1) of this part, unless the applicant: (1) Holds a flight instructor certificate or ground instructor certificate issued under this part;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Which schoolteachers are exempt from the Fundamentals of Instructing knowledge test?
notes.back: Holders of a State, county, city or municipal teacher's certificate authorising teaching at 7th grade or higher.
notes.explanation: The level matters: a certificate limited to teaching below 7th grade does not qualify.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (e)(2)
notes.evidence: (2) Holds a teacher's certificate issued by a State, county, city, or municipality that authorizes the person to teach at an educational level of the 7th grade or higher; or
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Which college staff are exempt from the Fundamentals of Instructing knowledge test?
notes.back: People employed as teachers at an accredited college or university.
notes.explanation: Here it is the employment that counts, not a teaching certificate; the college or university must be accredited.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (e)(3)
notes.evidence: (3) Is employed as a teacher at an accredited college or university.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Priya teaches physics at an accredited university and holds a commercial pilot certificate with an instrument rating. Which knowledge tests does she need for her first flight instructor certificate with an airplane rating?
notes.back: B) The Flight Instructor Airplane test only
notes.choices:
A) Both the Fundamentals of Instructing and the Flight Instructor Airplane tests
B) The Flight Instructor Airplane test only
C) Neither: her university post exempts her from both
D) The Fundamentals of Instructing test only
notes.choicesExplained: A: teaching at an accredited university exempts her from the fundamentals test. D: that is the test she is exempt from. C: the exemption covers only the §61.185(a)(1) areas, not the aeronautical knowledge test.
notes.explanation: Her university post exempts her from the fundamentals test, but the aeronautical knowledge test in §61.183(f) has no such exemption.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (e)(3)
notes.evidence: (3) Is employed as a teacher at an accredited college or university. (f) Pass a knowledge test on the aeronautical knowledge areas listed in § 61.185(a)(2) and (a)(3) of this part that are appropriate to the flight instructor rating sought;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Besides the fundamentals of instructing, what knowledge test must a flight instructor applicant pass?
notes.back: A test on the §61.185(a)(2) and (a)(3) aeronautical knowledge areas appropriate to the instructor rating sought.
notes.explanation: For an airplane rating this is the Flight Instructor Airplane test; unlike the fundamentals test, no teaching background exempts anyone from it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (f)
notes.evidence: (f) Pass a knowledge test on the aeronautical knowledge areas listed in § 61.185(a)(2) and (a)(3) of this part that are appropriate to the flight instructor rating sought;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What endorsement must a flight instructor applicant receive before the practical test?
notes.back: A logbook endorsement from an authorized instructor on the §61.187(b) areas of operation for the rating sought.
notes.explanation: It is a second, separate endorsement from the one for the fundamentals of instructing in §61.183(d).
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (g)
notes.evidence: (g) Receive a logbook endorsement from an authorized instructor on the areas of operation listed in § 61.187(b) of this part, appropriate to the flight instructor rating sought;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Who must make the practical-test endorsement for a first-time flight instructor applicant?
notes.back: An instructor who meets §61.195(h), the qualifications for training initial flight instructor applicants.
notes.explanation: So not every instructor may recommend a first-time instructor applicant; the endorser must meet the extra §61.195(h) experience rules.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 26, page 18
notes.evidence: An instructor who meets the requirements of 14 CFR § 61.195(h) must make the endorsement for first-time flight instructor applicants.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Ben earned his flight instructor certificate 10 calendar months ago, has given 180 hours of flight training and has endorsed only two applicants for practical tests. May he sign the practical-test endorsement for Ali, a first-time flight instructor applicant?
notes.back: C) No: the endorser must meet §61.195(h), which he does not yet do
notes.choices:
A) Yes, once Ali has passed both knowledge tests
B) Yes: any current flight instructor may make it
C) No: the endorser must meet §61.195(h), which he does not yet do
D) Yes, if a Gold Seal instructor countersigns
notes.choicesExplained: B: for first-time applicants the endorser must meet §61.195(h). A: passing the knowledge tests does not change who may endorse. D: the rules provide no countersignature route.
notes.explanation: Ben has neither 24 calendar months and 200 hours, nor five endorsed applicants, nor an enhanced qualification programme graduation.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 26, page 18
notes.evidence: An instructor who meets the requirements of 14 CFR § 61.195(h) must make the endorsement for first-time flight instructor applicants.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: The §61.183(i) endorsement states the applicant is competent and possesses instructional proficiency in stall awareness, {{c1::spin entry, spins, and spin recovery procedures}}.
notes.explanation: The endorsement is about the ability to teach these manoeuvres, given after flight training in them.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (i)(1)
notes.evidence: indicating that the applicant is competent and possesses instructional proficiency in stall awareness, spin entry, spins, and spin recovery procedures after providing the applicant with flight training in those training areas
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: In what aircraft must a flight instructor applicant's spin training be given?
notes.back: An airplane or glider, as appropriate, that is certificated for spins.
notes.explanation: The endorsement follows actual flight training in these areas, and the rule requires a spin-certificated aircraft for it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (i)(1)
notes.evidence: after providing the applicant with flight training in those training areas in an airplane or glider, as appropriate, that is certificated for spins; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: On a flight instructor airplane practical test, how can the spin endorsement affect the spin demonstration?
notes.back: The examiner may accept the endorsement as satisfactory evidence of instructional proficiency in stall awareness and spins.
notes.explanation: The word is 'may': acceptance is the examiner's choice, and it is not available on a spin-related retest.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (i)(2)
notes.evidence: upon presentation of the endorsement specified in paragraph (i)(1) of this section an examiner may accept that endorsement as satisfactory evidence of instructional proficiency in stall awareness, spin entry, spins, and spin recovery procedures for the practical test
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Lee failed a flight instructor airplane practical test on his spin recovery teaching. For the retest he brings a fresh spin-training endorsement. What must the examiner do?
notes.back: A) Test him on stall awareness, spin entry, spins and spin recovery in an aircraft certificated for spins
notes.choices:
A) Test him on stall awareness, spin entry, spins and spin recovery in an aircraft certificated for spins
B) Accept the endorsement, as on a first test
C) Leave spins out, since the endorsement shows retraining
D) Test spins orally, on the ground only
notes.choicesExplained: B: acceptance is not allowed on a spin-related retest. C: the rule says the examiner must test him. D: the test must be in an airplane or glider certificated for spins.
notes.explanation: A retest caused by spin-teaching deficiencies removes the examiner's option to accept the endorsement instead.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (i)(2)
notes.evidence: If the retest is a result of deficiencies in the ability of an applicant to demonstrate knowledge or skill of stall awareness, spin entry, spins, or spin recovery instructional procedures, the examiner must test the person on stall awareness, spin entry, spins, and spin recovery instructional procedures in an airplane or glider
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Does an applicant whose first flight instructor certificate will carry only an airplane multiengine rating need the spin endorsement?
notes.back: Yes: AC 61-65K says the spin endorsement still applies.
notes.explanation: The requirement attaches to the airplane category, so the multiengine class does not remove it.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 26.1, page 18
notes.evidence: This means, even if the applicant were to initially seek a flight instructor certificate with an airplane multiengine rating, the applicant would still be required to receive a logbook endorsement
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: A commercial helicopter pilot applies for a flight instructor certificate with a helicopter rating. What does §61.183(i) say about the spin endorsement?
notes.back: A) It is not required: it applies to airplane and glider instructor ratings
notes.choices:
A) It is not required: it applies to airplane and glider instructor ratings
B) It is required, in a helicopter certificated for spins
C) It is required only if he also holds an airplane rating
D) It is replaced by a stall-only endorsement
notes.choicesExplained: B: the paragraph does not cover helicopter ratings. C: the trigger is the instructor rating sought, not other ratings he holds. D: the paragraph sets no helicopter substitute.
notes.explanation: Paragraph (i) opens by limiting itself to airplane and glider ratings.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (i)
notes.evidence: (i) Accomplish the following for a flight instructor certificate with an airplane or a glider rating:
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: How much pilot-in-command time must a flight instructor applicant log, and in what?
notes.back: At least 15 hours as PIC in the category and class appropriate to the instructor rating sought.
notes.explanation: The hours must match the category and class of the rating sought, so total time elsewhere does not count toward it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (j)
notes.evidence: (j) Log at least 15 hours as pilot in command in the category and class of aircraft that is appropriate to the flight instructor rating sought; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Mia, a commercial pilot with an instrument rating, has 900 hours in all but only 12 hours as PIC in multiengine airplanes. Her first flight instructor certificate is to have an airplane multiengine rating. Which requirement does she not yet meet?
notes.back: C) 15 hours as PIC in the category and class sought
notes.choices:
A) The instrument rating requirement
B) The minimum age
C) 15 hours as PIC in the category and class sought
D) 5 hours as PIC in the make and model
notes.choicesExplained: A: she already holds an instrument rating. B: nothing suggests she is under 18. D: the 5-hour make-and-model rule limits which multiengine training an instructor may give (§61.195(f)); it is not an eligibility rule.
notes.explanation: Her 900 hours do not help: the 15 hours must be in the category and class of the instructor rating sought.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.183 Eligibility requirements (eCFR), paragraph (j)
notes.evidence: (j) Log at least 15 hours as pilot in command in the category and class of aircraft that is appropriate to the flight instructor rating sought; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: The fundamentals-of-instructing areas in §61.185(a)(1) open with {{c1::the learning process}}, followed by elements of effective teaching.
notes.explanation: It comes first in the regulation's list; the knowledge test in §61.183(e) covers the same six areas.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(1)
notes.evidence: the fundamentals of instructing, including: (i) The learning process; (ii) Elements of effective teaching; (iii) Student evaluation and testing; (iv) Course development; (v) Lesson planning; and (vi) Classroom training techniques.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: In §61.185(a)(1), the fundamentals-of-instructing area after the learning process is {{c1::elements of effective teaching}}.
notes.explanation: The applicant must receive and log ground training on it from an authorized instructor.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(1)
notes.evidence: the fundamentals of instructing, including: (i) The learning process; (ii) Elements of effective teaching; (iii) Student evaluation and testing; (iv) Course development; (v) Lesson planning; and (vi) Classroom training techniques.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: In §61.185(a)(1), the area between elements of effective teaching and course development is {{c1::student evaluation and testing}}.
notes.explanation: It is the only one of the six areas about assessing learners rather than preparing or giving instruction.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(1)
notes.evidence: the fundamentals of instructing, including: (i) The learning process; (ii) Elements of effective teaching; (iii) Student evaluation and testing; (iv) Course development; (v) Lesson planning; and (vi) Classroom training techniques.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: In §61.185(a)(1), the area between student evaluation and testing and lesson planning is {{c1::course development}}.
notes.explanation: Course development and lesson planning sit side by side, from the whole course down to the single lesson.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(1)
notes.evidence: the fundamentals of instructing, including: (i) The learning process; (ii) Elements of effective teaching; (iii) Student evaluation and testing; (iv) Course development; (v) Lesson planning; and (vi) Classroom training techniques.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: In §61.185(a)(1), the area between course development and classroom training techniques is {{c1::lesson planning}}.
notes.explanation: Holders of an instructor certificate, qualifying schoolteachers and college teachers are exempt from this training under §61.185(b).
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(1)
notes.evidence: the fundamentals of instructing, including: (i) The learning process; (ii) Elements of effective teaching; (iii) Student evaluation and testing; (iv) Course development; (v) Lesson planning; and (vi) Classroom training techniques.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: The sixth fundamentals-of-instructing area in §61.185(a)(1), after lesson planning, is {{c1::classroom training techniques}}.
notes.explanation: With it the list of six areas that make up the fundamentals-of-instructing ground training is complete.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(1)
notes.evidence: the fundamentals of instructing, including: (i) The learning process; (ii) Elements of effective teaching; (iii) Student evaluation and testing; (iv) Course development; (v) Lesson planning; and (vi) Classroom training techniques.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: A ground lesson teaches a new instructor how to write fair written questions and grade a learner's answers. Which §61.185(a)(1) fundamentals area does it belong to?
notes.back: Student evaluation and testing.
notes.explanation: Writing and grading test questions is assessment work, which is what this area covers among the six.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(1)
notes.evidence: the fundamentals of instructing, including: (i) The learning process; (ii) Elements of effective teaching; (iii) Student evaluation and testing; (iv) Course development; (v) Lesson planning; and (vi) Classroom training techniques.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: The aeronautical knowledge areas of which pilot certificates must a flight instructor applicant be trained on?
notes.back: Those of the recreational, private and commercial pilot certificates, for the aircraft category sought.
notes.explanation: The applicant's ground training spans every certificate level from recreational to commercial within that category.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(2)
notes.evidence: (2) The aeronautical knowledge areas for a recreational, private, and commercial pilot certificate applicable to the aircraft category for which flight instructor privileges are sought; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: An airplane instructor applicant who already holds a commercial pilot certificate asks whether she can skip ground training on recreational and private pilot knowledge areas. What does §61.185 say?
notes.back: No: she must receive and log ground training on the recreational, private and commercial areas for the airplane category.
notes.explanation: The rule lists all three certificate levels; holding the highest one does not remove the lower ones from the training.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.185 Aeronautical knowledge (eCFR), paragraph (a)(2)
notes.evidence: (2) The aeronautical knowledge areas for a recreational, private, and commercial pilot certificate applicable to the aircraft category for which flight instructor privileges are sought; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must a flight instructor applicant's logbook show about the §61.187 areas of operation?
notes.back: Logged flight and ground training on them from an authorized instructor, and an endorsement that the applicant is proficient to pass the practical test.
notes.explanation: This is the training behind the practical-test endorsement required by §61.183(g).
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.187 Flight proficiency (eCFR), paragraph (a)
notes.evidence: must receive and log flight and ground training from an authorized instructor on the areas of operation listed in this section that apply to the flight instructor rating sought. The applicant's logbook must contain an endorsement from an authorized instructor certifying that the person is proficient to pass a practical test on those areas of operation.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: The first airplane single-engine area of operation in §61.187(b)(1) is {{c1::Fundamentals of instructing}}, followed by technical subject areas.
notes.explanation: The list begins with teaching itself before any flying subject.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.187 Flight proficiency (eCFR), paragraph (b)(1)

notes.front: How can a military instructor pilot establish flight instructor recent experience?

notes.back: In the previous 24 calendar months, at least 10 applicants trained and recommended for a practical test, with at least 80% passing first time.

notes.front: What examining record qualifies an instructor for a Gold Seal?
notes.back: In the previous 24 calendar months, at least 20 practical tests as an examiner, or graduation tests as chief instructor of a part 141 course.
notes.explanation: It rewards examining as well as training, as an alternative to the 10-applicant record.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 28, page 21
